Subject: sudden latency & retry storms after SDK 3.4.0

Hi Soojin,

We pushed the client SDK 3.4.0 to production at ~08:55 PT and immediately started seeing a large spike in p99 latency for our live checkout stream. Error rate climbed from ~0.5% to ~8% and throughput dropped (many clients reporting duplicated attempts). The logs show repeated CONNECT/STREAM retries and a lot of partial header fragments. Sample logs attached below:

[snip] 2027-09-09T08:59:13Z INFO connection: reconnecting, reason=parser_error, fragment_len=12
[snip] 2027-09-09T08:59:13Z WARN request: retrying(3) id=0x7f12

We rolled back to 3.3.2 at 09:05 PT which reduced retries but some customers still see elevated p99s. Can you research ASAP? We're seeing customer impact (live payments).

Jill

Subject: Re: sudden latency & retry storms after SDK 3.4.0 — quick analysis

I replayed the fragments Jill attached against our streaming parser. Short summary: SDK 3.4.0 introduced a more aggressive frame coalescer that tries to reduce syscall count by merging header bytes. Under certain TCP Nagle/window conditions that leads to header boundary splits being reported as zero-length header suffixes. The parser treats those zero-length suffixes as an error and signals the client to reconnect/retry. When many clients do this at once, the backend sees a thundering set of short-lived connections and p99 skyrockets.

Repro steps (local):
1) netem delay 30ms + small MTU -> produce fragmented header sequence A
2) run SDK 3.4.0 with coalescer enabled: observe parser_error + immediate retry

Temporary mitigations to push now:
- Disable the coalescer flag in the SDK binary (runtime toggle exists) — avoids creating those zero-length fragment cases.
- Increase parser fragment timeout from 50ms -> 250ms so parser will wait for the rest of the header instead of erroring.
- As a fallback, allow server-side accept of fragment-continued packets for a short window (we can do this on the edge router).

Long-term: revert the coalescer change and add a fuzz harness in CI that simulates fragmented headers and validates no error path is hit.

I’ve attached a small patch that toggles the runtime flag (sdk-config-diff.patch). I’ll prepare a quick hotfix build if we want to cut 3.4.1.

—Ben

Date: 2027-09-09T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Update: mitigation applied (parser wait window + disabled coalescer)

Hi Jill — quick update from the war room: we applied two mitigations at 11:05 PT: disabled the client-side coalescer via runtime flag and increased the parser fragment wait window from 50ms to 250ms on the edge. We also accepted fragment-continued packets for a 60s window to allow in-flight clients to finish exchanges.

Early telemetry shows retries dropping to baseline and p99 improving ~60% vs the peak. Could you validate from your side whether checkout throughput and error rates have normalized for affected customers?

We’ve attached a diagnostics bundle and the config diff we applied. We will cut a 3.4.1 hotfix that removes the coalescer and add a regression test for fragmented headers to CI.

Attachments: diagnostics_bundle_20270909.zip (log pack, parser traces), sdk-config-diff.patch (runtime flag toggle)

Deeply sorry for the impact — we will include a formal postmortem and recommended remediation steps within 48 hours.

— Soojin
